name: Ashtadasha Maha Shakti Peethas
theme: The eighteen great seats of the Goddess across the subcontinent, named in the hymn ascribed to Adi Shankara
description: The Shakti Peethas are seats of the Goddess that, in the widely told legend, arose where parts of the body of Sati fell as Shiva bore her through the worlds after Daksha's sacrifice. The Ashtadasha Shakti Peetha Stotram, ascribed to Adi Shankara, names eighteen of them as the greatest. This circuit follows the order of the hymn: Shankari in Lanka and Kamakshi at Kanchipuram; Shrinkhala in Bengal; the Deccan seats of Chamundeshwari, Jogulamba and Bhramaramba, Mahalakshmi of Kolhapur and Ekaveera of Mahur; Mahakali at Ujjain, Puruhutika at Pithapuram, Girija at Jajpur and Manikyamba at Draksharamam; then Kamakhya in Assam, Madhaveswari at Prayag, Jwalamukhi's eternal flames, Mangala Gauri at Gaya, Vishalakshi at Kashi, and Sharada in far Kashmir. It spans the whole subcontinent and is most sacred during Navaratri.
